body:
OBSERVED in source, 2026-08-23.

Classic's TXT reader is paged: `cps/templates/readtxt.html:28-32` renders left/right arrows
around the text, and `cps/static/js/reading/txt_reader.js:27-65` binds arrow keys, arrow
clicks, swipe and mouse wheel to `prevPage`/`nextPage`, which shift the `<pre>` by one content
width (`txt_reader.js:67-85`).

The SPA fetches the file and emits one continuously scrolling block:
`frontend/src/pages/NativeReader.tsx:33-41` (fetch) and `:70` (`<pre className={styles.text}>`).
No paging, no keyboard navigation, no arrows.

Stated honestly, this one is a product decision and not obviously a defect: classic's
implementation is crude (it offsets a `<pre>` and hijacks the wheel, so ordinary scrolling is
taken away), and continuous scroll is the better behaviour on touch. What is NOT defensible is
recording TXT as full parity — surface 33 is Partial, not Native.

Decide one of: reach interaction parity, or write down that paged TXT reading is retired
deliberately. Do not leave it recorded as equivalent.
title: New UI TXT reader has no paging; classic paginates with arrows, keys, swipe and wheel
